subject.title: Context pruning mode 'off' not preventing compactions (Anthropic API key, cache-ttl smart defaults)

question: Should OpenClaw add a supported hard-limit-only or fully-off automatic compaction contract, or keep current `default`/`safeguard` modes and treat low-context compactions only as trigger-accounting bugs?
rationale: Current main already fixes the most likely Anthropic aggregate-cache accounting path, but the remaining request changes compaction safety semantics and config surface.

options.title: Define Hard-Limit Semantics
options.body: Add an approved config contract that preserves overflow recovery while disabling threshold/safeguard compaction, plus trigger metadata, docs, and regression coverage.

options.title: Keep Current Modes
options.body: Do not add a new compaction mode; focus follow-up work on verified false low-context triggers and clearer docs for pruning versus compaction.

options.title: Wait For Live Anthropic Proof
options.body: Require a current-main Anthropic API-key reproduction before accepting new compaction semantics beyond the shipped context-usage fix.

recommendation.title: Define Hard-Limit Semantics
recommendation.body: Add an approved config contract that preserves overflow recovery while disabling threshold/safeguard compaction, plus trigger metadata, docs, and regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice crosses compaction safety, config compatibility, and session-state ownership where recent history points closest to steipete.
